altTaglines: For people who eat with intent.
The heat behind every great meal.
positioning: Gochujang is the culinary discovery platform for design-conscious home cooks and flavor obsessives — a place to find, save, and build a living map of the dishes, techniques, and ingredients worth chasing. Where recipe sites feel like utilitarian databases and food blogs feel like personal diaries, Gochujang is the editorially-sharp, visually-electric home base that treats your evolving taste as something worth curating beautifully.
brandStory: Gochujang starts with a jar of fermented chili paste — proof that patience, heat, and a point of view turn the ordinary into the unforgettable. We built Gochujang for the cook who reads menus like novels and remembers meals like milestones. This isn't a shelf of recipes; it's a place to chase flavor with intent — to discover the dish you didn't know you needed, track the ones that changed you, and watch your taste sharpen over time. Global by instinct, bold by design. Bring your appetite. We'll bring the heat.
voiceTone: Confident, warm, and vivid — the voice of a well-traveled friend who happens to be a brilliant cook and an even better editor. Short, punchy sentences that pop like a first bite; sensory verbs over adjectives; specificity over hype. We name the char, the ferment, the exact chili — never "delicious." We have taste and we share it plainly: opinionated but never snobbish, playful but never gimmicky. We invite, we never lecture. Headlines run loud and declarative; body copy slows down and gets tactile. Second person, active voice, zero corporate filler.
valueProps: Discover dishes worth chasing — an editorially-curated feed of standout recipes, techniques, and ingredients across global cuisines, not an endless undifferentiated database
Track your evolving taste — save, rate, and organize the meals that matter into a beautiful living collection you actually want to revisit
See your palate grow — every dish you log sharpens a personal flavor map that surfaces smarter, bolder suggestions over time
Cook with confidence — clear, technique-forward guidance that respects your intelligence and your time
A feed that feels designed, not dumped — every screen reads like a premium food magazine spread
differentiators: Discovery-first, not search-first: an editorial point of view curates what you see instead of dumping a search index on you
Tracking as identity, not admin: your saved dishes form a curated taste profile, framed as a badge of who you are as an eater
Magazine-grade art direction on every surface — the anti-'boring tracker' — where competitors ship spreadsheet UX
Global and cross-cuisine by default, unbounded by a single-region or single-diet niche
Palate intelligence that compounds: recommendations get sharper the more you engage, turning a tool into a relationship
targetAudience: Design-conscious home cooks and food lovers aged roughly 25-45 who treat cooking as a creative pursuit and a form of self-expression. They screenshot restaurant menus, follow chefs on Instagram, own the good knife and the natural wine, and can taste the difference between fish sauce brands. They're globally curious, aesthetically demanding, and quietly competitive about their palate. They abandon utilitarian recipe sites because those sites feel beneath their taste — they want a tool as considered and beautiful as the food they cook.
logoDirection: A custom wordmark 'Gochujang' set in a bold, high-contrast modern grotesque (think Neue Haas Grotesk Display Bold or a customized GT Sesano) — tight tracking, oversized, confident. The signature move: the dot of a lowercase 'j' (or a purpose-built ligature) rendered as a single glowing ember-red drop, a nod to the paste and the heat, doubling as a standalone app-icon brand mark. Primary lockup is all-caps or sentence-case wordmark in near-black on warm off-white, with the ember-red accent as the only color. For the icon/favicon: a rounded-square 'G' with a subtle vertical gradient from deep gochujang crimson to ember orange, optionally paired with a single stylized chili-glyph counter. Keep the mark flat, no gloss, no gradients on the wordmark itself — let color and weight do the shouting. Color anchors: near-black ink (#1A1310), warm bone paper (#F5EFE6), and the hero ember-crimson (#D6482B → #E86A2C gradient).
namingRationale: 'Gochujang' names the platform after Korea's fermented chili paste — an ingredient that is bold, deep, slow-built, and unmistakably itself. It signals heat and a point of view without boxing the brand into a single cuisine: the paste is the metaphor, not the menu. The word is phonetically distinctive, globally recognizable to food-forward audiences, and owns a memorable sound and a built-in color story (fermented crimson). It flags 'this is not a beige, everything-for-everyone recipe site' the moment you hear it — exactly the 5-second differentiation the brand needs.
